query: How should we define and enforce a strict held-out real-patch protocol (source exclusion by site/subject) to prevent synthetic-real leakage and what quantitative domain-gap tests will demonstrate no leakage?

response.query: How should we define and enforce a strict held-out real-patch protocol (source exclusion by site/subject) to prevent synthetic-real leakage and what quantitative domain-gap tests will demonstrate no leakage?
response.answer: To enforce a held-out real-patch protocol, exclude synthetic and real data by site/subject. Use domain-gap tests like feature distribution analysis and adversarial attacks to confirm no leakage. Ensure strict data separation and validation.

results.content: Subsequently, in proposed § 146.115(a), FAA would allow Service Level 1 providers to demonstrate compliance with the applicable certificate requirements using a declaration of compliance. Accordingly, FAA proposes in § 146.115(b), discussed in more detail in the following section, to require the service provider submit documentation describing how the applicant meets the requirements. Consistent with FAA's risk-based approach, FAA would require in proposed § 146.115(c) that applicants for Service Level 3 certification to submit documentation and supporting data demonstrating that the applicant meet applicable requirements. In that section, FAA proposes that each certificated service provider perform any software updates to their authorized service in accordance with proposed § 146.405, which includes its own set of requirements for releasing software changes and notifying FAA of those changes. As proposed in § 146.405(c), FAA would require a certificated automated data service provider to test any software changes they want to apply to their automated data service prior to releasing the updated service to their users.

results.title: Non-Compete Clause Rule
results.content: Specifically, the final rule provides that, with respect to a worker other than a senior executive, it is an unfair method of competition for a person to enter into or attempt to enter into a non-compete clause; to enforce or attempt to enforce a non-compete clause; or to represent that the worker is subject to a non-compete clause.[8]  The Commission describes the basis for its finding that these practices are unfair methods of competition in Parts IV.B.1 through IV.B.3. Estimated as 80% \* 18.1% \* 66% \* (33,271,644-27,151,987), where 80% is the percentage of covered workers (see Part X.F.4.a), 18.1% is the estimated percentage of workers with non-competes (see Starr, Prescott, & Bishara, *supra* note 68), 67% is the assumed percent of workers without digital contact information, and 6,119,657 = 33,271,644-27,151,987 is the count of workers at small businesses (see *https://advocacy.sba.gov/​wp-content/​uploads/​2023/​11/​2023-Small-Business-Economic-Profile-US.pdf*).
